## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.5 — settings screen, and profiles reach the UI

> **Alpha.** Exercised in a browser against a real bridge on Linux; not tested
> on Windows or macOS, and the Android APK has still never run on a phone. For
> something that has actually been used, stay on
> [v0.0.1](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/releases/tag/v0.0.1).

### A settings screen

`/settings.html`, reachable from the header. Profile, listen address,
authentication, and TLS, all editable without hand-writing
`~/.config/huemux/app.json`.

Two deliberate limits:

- **Changes are only accepted from the machine HueMux runs on.** Rewriting the
  listen address or switching authentication off is exactly the operation that
  should not be reachable from the network it governs. Remote viewers get a
  read-only page saying so. This checks the actual connection, not an
  `X-Forwarded-For` header — that is a caller-supplied string anything could
  set.
- **The auth token is never sent to the browser.** The page is told whether one
  exists, never what it is. Leave the field blank to keep the current token;
  type to replace it.

Anything fixed at bind time — listen address, TLS, profile — reports
"restart HueMux for this to take effect" rather than claiming success and
quietly doing nothing.

### Profiles now reach the UI

Until now `--profile=lights` gated the server but both tabs still appeared.
Now the disabled tab is gone, and — more usefully — its page is never loaded,
so it no longer opens a WebSocket to a UI nobody can reach.

A fix that came with it: a lights-only deployment opened at `/sync.html` used
to land on a frame that was never created and show a blank page. It now falls
back to whichever tab exists.

### Still not wired up

`--listen-host`, `--auth`, and `--tls` are settable and persisted, but the
server still binds `127.0.0.1` and does not yet enforce a token. Those are the
next phases — the settings screen is ready for them ahead of time.
